The marginal covariance of the response of a fitted model

Source: R/marginal_cov.R
fb_marginal_cov.Rd

Returns the covariance of the response over the rows of a fit's data, given its fitted variance components, $$V = R + \sum_k \sigma_k^2 Z_k G_k Z_k^\top + K,$$ as a structured object with one block per variance component. as.matrix() assembles it as a dense matrix.

Usage

fb_marginal_cov(fit, rows = NULL, variances = TRUE)

# S3 method for class 'fb_marginal_cov'
as.matrix(x, rows = NULL, cols = rows, ...)

Arguments

fit

A fitted flexybayes model, or an fb_marginal_cov object to take a subset of or to evaluate at other variances.

rows

Integer positions of the rows to cover: rows of the fit's data, or of fit when it is an fb_marginal_cov object. NULL (the default) covers every row.

variances

TRUE (the default) to use the fit's own variance components, FALSE for the structure alone, with every variance NA. or a list with residual (the residual variance, or one per section named by level), terms (a variance per block, named by block) and, for an AR1 x AR1 field, rho (a list of c(row = , col = ) named by block), all on the variance scale.

x

An fb_marginal_cov object.

cols

Integer positions of the columns, for a cross-covariance between two sets of rows. Defaults to rows.

...

Unused.

Value

An object of class fb_marginal_cov, a list with

n, rows

The number of rows covered, and their positions in the fit's data.

residual

A list: variance (one value, or one per section named by level), by (the sectioning column, or NULL), level (each row's section, or NULL), weights (each row's observation weight, or NULL) and known_variance (each row's known variance, or NULL).

blocks

A named list, one entry per variance component: name, label, component (the names the variance may carry in summary(fit)$varcomp), variance, index, n_levels, value, key, columns and structure as described above, and for an AR1 x AR1 field rho and kronecker, the factors n_at (trials), row and col (AR1 correlation matrices) with \(G = I_{n_{at}} \otimes R_{row} \otimes R_{col}\).

known_covariance

The known covariance matrix over the rows, whose diagonal is residual$known_variance, or NULL.

groups

Whether V is block-diagonal over a grouping column: applicable, column, blocks (row positions per group, the grouping with the most groups that every block nests within) and reason.

varcomp

The variance-component table the values were read from, or NULL.

Details

Each variance enters at its posterior mean, \(E[\sigma^2] = \mathrm{estimate}^2 + \mathrm{std.error}^2\), read from the fit's variance-component table, summary(fit)$varcomp, whose estimate and std.error are the posterior mean and standard deviation of each standard deviation. For a structure without a correlation parameter this is the posterior mean of V itself. The two correlations of an AR1 x AR1 field enter at their posterior means (estimate). On brms, the rows of a sectioned residual report the posterior median of each standard deviation, so there the residual variances are median^2 + std.error^2.

The structures built are random intercepts ((1 | g), ide(g)), two-way interactions (a:b), uncorrelated random slopes ((x || g)), diag(f):g, an ar1(row):ar1(col) field on one trial or id(trial):ar1(row):ar1(col) on each trial, and vm() or ped() known covariances, over an independent residual or one variance per level of a factor (dsum(~ units | f)). Observation weights divide the residual variance (\(\sigma^2 / w_i\)), a known variance per row is added to it, and a known covariance matrix is added whole.

A model with any other structure is refused with the reason code marginal_cov_not_buildable, naming the terms.

See also

fb_variance_draws() for posterior draws of the variance components.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  d <- data.frame(site = factor(rep(1:6, each = 5)))
  d$y <- rnorm(6)[d$site] + rnorm(30)
  fit <- flexybayes(y ~ 1, random = ~site, data = d, backend = "inla",
                    verbose = FALSE)
  v <- fb_marginal_cov(fit, rows = 1:10)
  v$blocks$site$variance
  as.matrix(v)
}
